stories.headline: Flood fears rise with flyover plan at Puthukkad in Keralam
stories.title: Flood fears rise with flyover plan at Puthukkad in Keralam
stories.summary: Residents seek pillar-supported structure citing drainage disruption and growing vulnerability to waterlogging
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The proposed Puthukkad flyover on National Highway (NH) 544 in Keralam’s Thrissur has triggered serious environmental and flood-related concerns, with residents warning that the proposed 1.38-km earth-filled approach could turn the highway into a massive barrier to the natural flow of rainwater and aggravate flooding in the low-lying town and adjacent panchayats.
The Puthukkad Melpalam Janakeeya Samithi has demanded that the proposed flyover and its approach roads be constructed on pillars, instead of raising a long stretch of the highway with earth.

According to the project proposal, only about 70 metres at the Puthukkad Signal Junction would remain open at ground level, while nearly 1,380 metres would be built on an earth-filled embankment, points out the Samithi.
It argues that such a structure could obstruct natural drainage between the low-lying areas on either side of the highway.
“Puthukkad is located in a geographically sensitive area where water movement cannot be treated as a secondary consideration.
A long earth embankment could become a physical barrier to the natural flow of floodwater,” said Seby Kodiyan, chairperson of the Samithi.
The concern assumes significance against the backdrop of the region’s history of waterlogging during periods of intense rainfall.

K. K. Aneesh Kumar of the Kerala Sasthra Sahithya Parishad (KSSP) has pointed to the flooding in Puthukkad during the 2018 and 2019 deluges and instances of waterlogging reported during heavy rain in subsequent years.
When the Peechi dam was opened without warning in 2024, Amballur and Puthukkad bore the brunt of floods, he said.
How will the water flowing down from the eastern hills and low-lying areas make its way westward after being obstructed by the Amballur and Puthukkad flyovers, built in close proximity to each other?
This is the question raised by the KSSP activists, who conducted a study of the region.
“The ecological implications of altering the existing drainage pattern needs to be studied comprehensively before the project design is finalised.

stories.headline: SC issues notice to Congress, Rahul Gandhi over march to court, posts against CJI
stories.title: SC issues notice to Congress, Rahul Gandhi over march to court, posts against CJI
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notice to the Congress, Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders on a plea seeking restrictions on political demonstrations in court premises following the Opposition’s march to the apex court on October 12 and social media posts targeting Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi sought responses to the petition filed by four lawyers. Senior Advocate Gaurav Bhatia, appearing for the petitioners, argued that demonstrations within court premises amounted to an attempt to intimidate the judiciary. “Nobody can browbeat the judiciary,” the CJI observed. “We are not sitting in ivory towers. We know what statements they are making outside and what they are saying in Court. We know everything,” he said. The petition also sought criminal contempt action against the Congress’s Kerala unit over an X post that told the CJI to resign and said the party would find his replacement. However, the bench declined to issue notice on the contempt plea at this stage. “No contempt today. We are only issuing notice. Let us see what the response is, and then we will take it forward,” the CJI said, according to Bar & Bench. The plea also named Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav among the respondents.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Upholds Madras HC Verdict Declaring TN Quota for Muslim Converts Unconstitutional
stories.title: Supreme Court Upholds Madras HC Verdict Declaring TN Quota for Muslim Converts Unconstitutional
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a Madras High Court judgment declaring unconstitutional a Tamil Nadu government order allowing people from Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes, Denotified Communities and Scheduled Castes to claim Backward Class (Muslim) reservation benefits after converting to Islam.

A Bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar dismissed the Tamil Nadu government's special leave petition (SLP) challenging the Madras High Court's judgment, which had struck down the government order issued on March 9, 2024.

The apex court upheld the high court's ruling on constitutional principles, holding that a person belonging to a Backward Class or Scheduled Caste in the Hindu social order cannot automatically carry forward the benefit of reservation after embracing another religion.

The Supreme Court observed that social backwardness associated with a person's original religious and caste identity cannot simply be transferred to a different religious community following conversion.
The case arose from a plea filed by Sameer Ahamed N., who was born into a Hindu family and converted to Islam in 2015.
He subsequently sought a community certificate recognising him as a Muslim Lebbai, but his application was rejected by the revenue authorities in Tamil Nadu.

The Madras High Court had upheld the rejection and declared unconstitutional the Government Order (G.O.) No. 31, issued on March 9, 2024, which permitted converts from BC, MBC, Denotified Communities and Scheduled Castes to be treated as Backward Class Muslims for reservation purposes.
In its judgment, the High Court said the government could not use an executive order to override binding judicial precedents governing the consequences of conversion to Islam.

"When a Hindu gets converted to Islam, he becomes just a Mussalman, and his place in Muslim society is not determined by the caste to which he belonged before his conversion," a Division Bench of Justices G.R. Swaminathan and P.B. Balaji had observed, referring to an earlier Madras High Court judgment.

The high court further held that the government order was arbitrary because it sought to accommodate people from distinct reservation categories, including Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes, within the same category of Backward Class Muslims.
The Madras High Court concluded that a person converting to Islam could not claim membership of one of the notified Backward Class Muslim communities merely on the basis of conversion.
"As a corollary, we hold that a convert to Islam cannot claim the status of Backward Class Muslim.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks Sanjay Raut To Explain Remarks Against CJI & Judges While Entertaining INDIA Bloc Petition
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks Sanjay Raut To Explain Remarks Against CJI & Judges While Entertaining INDIA Bloc Petition
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (October 15) asked Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut to explain his remarks against the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and the judiciary while entertaining the petition filed by INDIA bloc leaders against the Election Commission of India (ECI).

In its order, the bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said that the petition was being provisionally entertained at Raut's instance, subject to him explaining his conduct.

Incidentally, Attorney General R Venkataramani granted consent yesterday to the Supreme Court Bar Association to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Raut over his comments concerning the judiciary and CJI Surya Kant.

Raut had criticised the CJI for declining a meeting with Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, who had sought to meet the Chief Justice to raise concerns over alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Raut alleged that the CJI and several judges including the CJI had played badminton in London with BJP leaders and attended dinner parties with BJP ministers, but the CJI could not meet the Opposition leader.
During Thursday's hearing, the CJI had remarked that one of the petitioners would have to explain his conduct.
The CJI also observed that the judges were aware of statements being made outside the courtroom and were not living in "ivory towers".

While giving consent for criminal contempt proceedings, the Attorney General stated that Raut's statement on judges playing badminton with Ministers was false, and cited a Delhi High Court order which established this.
The AG also said that Raut's comments lowered the dignity of the judiciary and were scandalous in nature.
The petition was filed by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 11 other INDIA bloc leaders challenging the Election Commission's actions in connection with the SIR of electoral rolls.

Apart from Congress leaders Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, Saugata Roy (Trinamool Congress-Mamata Banerjee), Akhilesh Yadav (Samajwadi Party), Tejashwi Prasad Yadav (RJD), Sanjay Raut (Shiv Sena UBT), MA Baby (CPI(M)), D Raja (CPI), Mahua Majhi (JMM), Supriya Sule (NCP Sharad Pawar) and ET Muhammed Basheer (IUML) are the other petitioners.

stories.headline: 'Whether There Are Classes Among Journalists Who Require Additional Protection' : Supreme Court In Delhi Protest Matter
stories.title: 'Whether There Are Classes Among Journalists Who Require Additional Protection' : Supreme Court In Delhi Protest Matter
stories.summary: SG Tushar Mehta said everybody with a mic claims to be a journalist, and it has become difficult to distinguish journalists from 'reel-makers'.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: SG Tushar Mehta said everybody with a mic claims to be a journalist, and it has become difficult to distinguish journalists from 'reel-makers'.
In the Delhi Protest matter, the Supreme Court yesterday orally observed that journalists can be divided into certain classes, some of whom may require an additional level of protection.
The Court however said that it was not presiding on the issue as to 'who is a journalist'.
"We are not presiding that.
That would require a very detailed examination of whether freedom of expression will empower every citizen of this country to be a journalist?
That becomes difficult.

There will be layers of protection - whether they are accredited journalists, whether they are employed with media houses who are registered under Press Council, whether they are individual freelance journalists, whether they are influencers, etc...well aware that [there are] classes amongst journalists, we'd have to examine", Justice Joymalya Bagchi said.
The petitioner-side urged that is a larger issue, submissions on which can be made at an appropriate stage.
CJI Surya Kant then commented, "We will also keep in mind that if everybody will start claiming [they are] journalists, it will lead to creating problems".

A bench of CJI Kant and Justice Bagchi was dealing with petitions seeking reliefs for journalists who were allegedly manhandled during the protests and whose devices were allegedly seized by the authorities.
The pleas particularly claimed sexual harassment of women journalists, saying they were not only obstructed in performing their duties but also molested by male police officers.
One of the petitions, argued by Senior Advocate Indira Jaising, sought protection for all women journalists from any coercive action over the protest-coverage.
